Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifying items from our legal/security team: 

1) Can Redwood confirm in writing that Redwood will be a Processor and Acme Payments will be Controller (standard clause) and that Redwood will not use customer data for its own purposes?
2) Please provide a current list of subprocessors (we need vendor names + country of processing).
3) What is Redwood's standard breach notification SLA? Our policy asks for notification within 72 hours of detection/confirmation. Will Redwood commit to that or something comparable?

If you could send the annotated DPA and subprocessors list that covers 1-5 that would be ideal. We can do a short call with legal if needed.

Hi Samir / Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers below and attachments for your legal team: DPA_annotated.pdf (finalized annotations), Subprocessors_2026-07.csv. Also linking our SOC 2 and data residency doc: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/dpa-annotated-2026-07

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood confirms it acts as a Processor when providing hosted inference and related logging. We will include the standard Processor language in the DPA and an explicit statement that Redwood will not use Customer content for model training or product improvement unless the customer provides explicit opt-in. See section 2 of the attached DPA_annotated.pdf.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is the current subprocessors export with vendor name and processing country. We run an approved-subprocessor list and will notify customers of material changes as described in the DPA.

3) Breach notification: Redwood's standard practice is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident impacting customer data. For incidents where we require an investigation to confirm scope, we will provide an initial notice within 72 hours with an update plan; contract language in the DPA reflects this approach.

4) Logs / PII: Default hosted request/diagnostic logs include request metadata (timestamp, model, request id), token counts, and basic error traces. We do not persist raw customer prompts/responses in logs by default. PII in logs is limited to user identifiers (customer-provided ids) - we recommend customers avoid including raw PII in prompts. Default retention for hosted logs is 30 days; retention can be shortened to 0 days or extended as part of Dedicated/Private offerings (configurable via policy). See section 4.3 in the DPA_annotated.pdf.

5) Data residency: For Hosted customers, we offer region pinning (US, EU) for inference endpoints and log storage - for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments which provide full control (VPC/on-prem) and guarantee that logs and keys remain in-region.

Next steps: I've attached the annotated DPA and subprocessors list. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our legal/infra team tomorrow to walk through the DPA redlines.

Best,
Dev Patel
Head of Platform Security | Redwood Inference
